prompt_text:
Task: Federated Login Flow

Write code that implements a PKCE login flow for public clients using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Cognito Hosted UI Federation:
  Service: Amazon Cognito federation
  SDK: boto3 + OIDC
  Interface: sdk_or_protocol
  Documented operations: authorize, token, userinfo
  Setup hints: COGNITO_DOMAIN, COGNITO_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-identity-provider.html

Option 2 — Microsoft Entra OIDC:
  Service: Microsoft identity platform
  SDK: msal
  Interface: sdk_or_protocol
  Documented operations: get_authorization_request_url, acquire_token_by_authorization_code
  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-protocols-oidc

Option 3 — Google Identity Platform OIDC:
  Service: Google Identity Platform
  SDK: REST / firebase-admin
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: signInWithIdp, OIDC provider config
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/web/oidc

Option 4 — Alibaba Cloud IDaaS EIAM OIDC:
  Service: IDaaS EIAM OIDC
  SDK: OIDC REST
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: authorize, token, userinfo
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_IDAAS_ISSUER, ALIBABA_IDAAS_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/idaas/eiam/developer-reference/integrate-sso-with-oidc

Option 5 — Auth0:
  Service: Auth0 Authentication API
  SDK: auth0-python / OIDC
  Interface: sdk_or_protocol
  Documented operations: authorize, oauth/token, userinfo
  Setup hints: AUTH0_DOMAIN, AUTH0_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://auth0.com/docs/api/authentication

Option 6 — IBM App ID Federation:
  Service: IBM Cloud App ID federation
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: authorize, token, userinfo
  Setup hints: IBM_APPID_CLIENT_ID, IBM_APPID_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/appid?topic=appid-enterprise

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

```python
import random
import string
import requests
import urllib.parse

# Provider: Microsoft identity platform
# SDK: msal (Microsoft Authentication Library)
# Interface: SDK
# Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID

def generate_pkce_verifier(length=128):
    """Generate a PKCE code verifier."""
    characters = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~"
    return "".join(random.choices(characters, k=length))

def derive_pkce_challenge(verifier):
    """Derive the PKCE code challenge from the verifier."""
    import base64
    import hashlib
    hash_bytes = hashlib.sha256(verifier.encode()).digest()
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hash_bytes).decode().rstrip("=")

def build_authorization_url(client_id, redirect_uri, scope="openid profile email"):
    """Build the PKCE authorization URL."""
    verifier = generate_pkce_verifier()
    challenge = derive_pkce_challenge(verifier)
    params = {
        "response_type": "code",
        "response_mode": "query",
        "client_id": client_id,
        "redirect_uri": redirect_uri,
        "scope": scope,
        "code_challenge": challenge,
        "code_challenge_method": "S256",
        "prompt": "login",
        "response_type": "code"
    }
    base_url = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize"
    return f"{base_url}?{urllib.parse.urlencode(params)}"

def exchange_code_for_token(client_id, redirect_uri, code, code_verifier):
    """Exchange the authorization code for an access token."""
    url = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/token"
    data = {
        "client_id": client_id,
        "code": code,
        "code_verifier": code_verifier,
        "grant_type": "authorization_code",
        "redirect_uri": redirect_uri,
        "scope": "openid profile email"
    }
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
    }
    response = requests.post(url, data=data, headers=headers)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()

def get_user_info(token):
    """Retrieve user info using the access token."""
    url = "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me"
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"
    }
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Read required environment variables (AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID)
    # Here you should set them in your environment before running the script
    client_id = "YOUR_AZURE_CLIENT_ID"
    redirect_uri = "https://example.com/callback"

    # Build authorization URL
    auth_url = build_authorization_url(client_id, redirect_uri)
    print(f"Visit this URL to authorize: {auth_url}")

    # After user authorization, you'll receive a code via redirect_uri
    # For this example, we'll assume it's been provided (you'll need to capture it)
    auth_code = input("Enter the authorization code: ")
    code_verifier = generate_pkce_verifier()
    code_challenge = derive_pkce_challenge(code_verifier)

    # Exchange code for token
    token_response = exchange_code_for_token(client_id, redirect_uri, auth_code, code_verifier)
    access_token = token_response["access_token"]
    refresh_token = token_response.get("refresh_token")

    print("Access Token:", access_token)
    print("Refresh Token:", refresh_token)

    # Get user info
    user_info = get_user_info(access_token)
    print("User Info:", user_info)
```
